title: Notitia: Rome grants apprehension, explicit chief articles, and useful growth in knowledge
source_text: LX. Quod attinet ad fidei actus, quaeritur primo de notitia & cognitione rerum credendarum, An & quousque ad fidem pertineat & necessaria sit? Concedunt autem, ut ante visum est, Reformatis Doctores Scholae Romanae ad fidem concipiendam aliquam objecti credendi conceptionem & apprehensionem necessariam esse: imo ad fidem salvificam requiri expressam atque explicitam praecipuorum aliquot articulorum fidei notitiam. Denique, etsi dicant ad salutem sufficere plerorumque dogmatum religionis fidem implicitam, imo praecipuorum ipsorum mysteriorum rudem & confusam tantum cognitionem, non negant tamen utilem & laudabilem esse distinctiorem & accuratiorem notitiam rerum divinarum, ut quae magis ac magis animos in Dei amorem accendat: ac proinde fideles hortationibus posse & debere compelli, ut pro modo vocationis, & singulorum captu, in mysteriorum fidei notitia magis ac magis proficiant.
pass_a_gloss: As for the acts of faith, it is asked first concerning knowledge and cognition of things to be believed — whether and how far it belongs to faith and is necessary. But the Doctors of the Roman school concede to the Reformed, as was seen before, that for conceiving faith some conception and apprehension of the object to be believed is necessary; indeed that for saving faith an expressed and explicit knowledge of some principal articles of faith is required. Finally, although they say that for salvation an implicit faith of most dogmas of religion suffices, and even only a rude and confused cognition of the principal mysteries themselves, yet they do not deny that a more distinct and accurate knowledge of divine things is useful and praiseworthy, as that which more and more kindles souls in the love of God: and therefore the faithful can and ought to be urged by exhortations to advance more and more in the knowledge of the mysteries of faith according to the mode of their calling and each person capacity.
pass_b_english: On notitia Rome grants Reformed that some apprehension is needed to conceive faith, and explicit knowledge of chief articles for saving faith.
Implicit or rude cognition may suffice for many dogmas, yet clearer knowledge is useful and praiseworthy and should be pressed according to calling and capacity.

choices.why: Shared necessity of some apprehension plus growth.
